sections.title: GULF STATES
sections.text: SFC FRONT IS EXPECTED TO SAG SEWD ACROSS WRN TN INTO SRN AR EARLY IN THE PERIOD IN THE WAKE OF SHORTWAVE TROUGH EJECTING ACROSS THE OH VALLEY. WITH TIME...RENEWED SFC CYCLOGENESIS WILL DEVELOP ALONG THIS BOUNDARY DURING THE LATTER HALF OF THE PERIOD AS MID LEVEL SPEED MAX DIGS SEWD ACROSS OK INTO SRN AR. BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE HAS STEADILY INCREASED ACROSS THE CNTRL GULF COAST LATE THIS EVENING AS FAVORABLE LOW LEVEL TRAJECTORIES HAVE FORCED 60S SFC DEW POINTS AS FAR NORTH AS I-20 FROM NERN TX INTO CNTRL MS. THIS MOISTURE SURGE WILL OVERRUN THE AFOREMENTIONED SFC BOUNDARY AND THUNDERSTORMS WILL READILY DEVELOP WITHIN WARM ADVECTION REGIME BEGINNING EARLY IN THE PERIOD. LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR IS NOT EXPECTED TO BE PARTICULARLY STRONG OR FOCUSED...EXCEPT NEAR THE E-W FRONTAL ZONE WHERE DEEP SWLY FLOW WILL ENHANCE COOL SECTOR ELEVATED THUNDERSTORM POTENTIAL. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST THESE STORMS MAY PRODUCE HAIL GIVEN MODESTLY STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES. ADDITIONALLY...FORECAST PROFILES SUGGEST THE SRN HALF OF THE WARM SECTOR MAY REMAIN CAPPED...ESPECIALLY NEAR THE GULF COAST MUCH OF THE PERIOD. sections.title: CENTRAL GULF COAST STATES
sections.text: CURRENT LINE OF MARGINALLY SEVERE STORMS OVER KY/TN MAY CONTINUE TO POSE A RISK OF LOCALLY GUSTY/DAMAGING WINDS EARLY THIS MORNING. HOWEVER...A GREATER RISK IS EXPECTED TO EVOLVE FARTHER SOUTHWEST THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS PARTS OF AR/LA. A COMBINATION OF DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 60S...STEEPER MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES...AND COOL TEMPERATURES ALOFT WILL RESULT IN AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OVER 1000 J/KG. ISOLATED THUNDERSTORMS WILL LIKELY DEVELOP BY EARLY/MID AFTERNOON AND SPREAD EASTWARD INTO MS/AL DURING THE EVENING. FORECAST SOUNDINGS APPEAR FAVORABLE FOR LARGE /POSSIBLY SGFNT/ HAIL IN STRONGER CELLS. SUPERCELL STORMS WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE...LIKELY CAPABLE OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AS WELL.

sections.title: AR OVERNIGHT
sections.text: LATER THIS EVENING...STRONG LOW LEVEL WARM ADVECTION WILL DEVELOP ACROSS PARTS OF OK/AR AS NEXT UPPER TROUGH APPROACHES. THIS WILL LIKELY RESULT IN INCREASING COVERAGE OF ELEVATED THUNDERSTORMS OVERNIGHT. RELATIVELY STEEP LAPSE RATE WILL PROMOTE A RISK OF HAIL IN STRONGER CELLS...ALTHOUGH ORGANIZED SEVERE STORMS ARE NOT CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED. ..HART.. 02/27/2009

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: ONE STRONG S/WV TROUGH CURRENTLY OHIO VALLEY LIFTS NEWD ACROSS NEW ENGLAND TONIGHT WHILE A MUCH STRONGER COLD TROUGH OVER THE ROCKIES DEEPENS SEWD INTO CENTRAL PLAINS BY 12Z SAT. GULF MOISTURE CONTINUES TO SPREAD INLAND EWD ACROSS THE GULF STATES IN ADVANCE OF A MUCH COLDER AIR MASS. COLD FRONT OH VALLEY WILL CONTINUE EWD WITH TRAILING PORTION NOW INTO CENTRAL AR/NRN TX TENDING TO DECELERATE AS A SURFACE WAVE DEVELOPS LATER TONIGHT CENTRAL/NRN MS IN RESPONSE TO APPROACH OF DEEPENING UPSTREAM TROUGH/DEVELOPING UPPER LOW. ELEVATED MIXED LAYER IS SPREADING EWD ACROSS SRN PLAINS AND GULF STATES IN ADVANCE OF COLD FRONT...WHICH COUPLED WITH SURFACE DEWPOINTS RISING INTO THE LOW/MID 60S...PROVIDES AN ENVIRONMENT FAVORABLE FOR SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS...PARTICULARLY A LARGE HAIL THREAT.

sections.title: CENTRAL GULF STATES
sections.text: PREFRONTAL OVERNIGHT CONVECTION HAS SPREAD SEWD INTO NRN GULF STATES AND PROVIDES THE PRIMARY FOCUS FOR RENEWED NEAR SURFACE BASED SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT THIS MORNING. AT THE PRESENT TIME WITH MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES IN EXCESS OF 7C/KM AND WBZ GENERALLY AROUND 8K FEET...HAIL WILL BE COMMON IN STRONGER STORMS. WITH 50-60 KTS OF DEEP LAYER SHEAR...SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT WILL BECOME A GREATER CONCERN THIS AFTERNOON AS HEATING WEAKENS CINH AND MLCAPES CLIMB TO ABOVE 1000 J/KG ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR EWD INTO AL. THIS WILL NOT ONLY INCREASE THREAT OF LARGE DAMAGING HAIL BUT ALSO PROVIDE CONDITIONS FAVORABLE FOR TORNADOES. WHILE LOW LEVEL SHEAR IS NOT PARTICULARLY STRONG...GIVEN THE OTHER PARAMETERS IN PLACE ACROSS CENTRAL MS/AL BY THIS AFTERNOON...HAVE INCREASED THE TORNADO POTENTIAL IN THIS AREA. IN ADDITION SHORT LINE SEGMENTS/BOWS CURRENTLY WILL CONTINUE TO FORM ALONG AND N OF E/W BOUNDARY ACROSS NRN MS/AL WITH A WIND DAMAGE THREAT.

sections.title: ARKLATEX INTO CNTRL GULF COAST STATES
sections.text: 18Z MESOANALYSIS INDICATED SYNOPTIC FRONT EXTENDING FROM E OF BNA TO NEAR TUP TO TXK. AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY INTERSECTS THIS FRONT OVER S-CNTRL OR SERN AR...EXTENDING ESEWD ACROSS NRN MS /S OF GWO/ TO CNTRL AL /N OF MGM/. AS OF EARLY AFTERNOON...LARGE-SCALE SETUP CONTINUES TO FAVOR STORM REGENERATION NEAR THE INTERSECTION OF THE SYNOPTIC AND OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES OVER SRN AR WITH ADDITIONAL STORMS FORMING ALONG THE INCREASINGLY BAROCLINIC OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM NRN MS INTO CNTRL AL. 18Z SUPPLEMENTAL SOUNDINGS FROM JAN AND SHV INDICATE THAT A CAP AT THE BASE OF AN EML IS LARGELY INHIBITING TSTM DEVELOPMENT TO THE S OF ABOVE-MENTIONED OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ACROSS MUCH OF SYSTEM WARM SECTOR FROM ERN TX INTO CNTRL MS. THE EXCEPTION IS OVER CNTRL AL ON THE ERN EDGE OF EML WHERE CAP IS NOTABLY WEAKER /REF. 18Z BHM SOUNDING/. LATEST SHORT TERM MODEL GUIDANCE SUGGESTS THAT THE CORRIDOR FROM SRN AR INTO CNTRL AL WILL REMAIN THE PREFERRED ZONE FOR STORM REGENERATION THROUGH THE DIURNAL HEATING CYCLE. HERE...LOW-LEVEL WAA AND INCREASED FRONTOGENETICAL FORCING WILL SUPPORT VIGOROUS/ROTATING UPDRAFTS AS AIR MASS CONTINUES TO DESTABILIZE /I.E. MLCAPE APPROACHING 1000-1500 J PER KG/.
